links.outcome: Accuracy on multiple-choice exam vs open-ended and clinically modified questions
links.effect: MC answers 93.0%, reasoning 92.4%; open-ended answers 80.0%, reasoning 80.5% (p<0.001); modified MC answers 93.9% to 66.7%, reasoning 93.9% to 71.2% (both p<0.001).
links.quote: Using existing MC question formats substantially overestimates the performance and clinical reasoning capabilities of GPT o1-preview.

links.outcome: Accuracy after modifying critical clinical parameters in questions
links.effect: Modified MC accuracy fell from 93.9% to 66.7% for answers and to 71.2% for reasoning (both p<0.001); answer-reasoning concordance fell from 93.9% to 66.7% (p<0.001).
links.quote: For modified MC questions, accuracy decreased significantly (answers: 93.9% to 66.7%; reasoning: 93.9% to 71.2%; both p<0.001), as well as answer-reasoning concordance (93.9% to 66.7%, p<0.001).

unlisted_practices: Evaluating answer-reasoning concordance of LLM outputs

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating LLM performance on cardiology board exam questions across multiple-choice, open-ended, and perturbed contexts to reveal overestimation of clinical reasoning.
